gloss: sorry (es tut mir leid = I'm sorry)
notes: Es tut mir leid = I'm sorry. etwas leid sein = to be tired of something.

sentences.text: Tut mir leid, ich habe keine Zeit.
Das tut mir wirklich leid für dich.
Ich bin es leid, immer zu warten.

notes: Spoken short form: komm rein = come in.
Mostly spoken: Das ist halt so. Halt! on its own means Stop!

sentences.text: Dann machen wir es halt morgen.
sentences.translation: Then we'll just do it tomorrow.

notes: Like an adjective after a determiner: die beiden = the two of them.

sentences.text: Wir beide gehen heute ins Kino.
sentences.translation: The two of us are going to the cinema today.

sentences.text: Ich kenne die beiden schon lange.
sentences.translation: I've known the two of them for a long time.

notes: Plural: Sachen, often meaning things or stuff.
Hilfe! = Help!
Endings like der: jeder Mann, jede Frau, jedes Kind. On its own, jeder = everyone.

gloss: gladly; (with a verb) to like doing
notes: Ich esse gern Fisch = I like eating fish. Gern geschehen = You're welcome.

sentences.translation: Are you coming along? Yes, gladly!

notes: Replaces über + it/that: Ich denke darüber nach = I'm thinking about it.

sentences.translation: We need to talk about it.
The picture is hanging right above it.
What do you think about it?

gloss: to hold; to stop; (halten von) to think of
notes: du hältst, er hält; past hielt, gehalten. Was hältst du davon? = What do you think of it?

sentences.translation: Can you hold this for a moment?
What do you think of that?

notes: Past participle: verstanden. Verstanden? = Got it?
nicht wahr? = isn't it? (a tag question)

gloss: to it; for it; with it
notes: Replaces zu + it/that: Ich habe keine Lust dazu = I don't feel like it.

sentences.translation: What do you say to that?
I don't have time for it.
Would you like bread with it?

notes: Plural: Brüder.

sentences.text: Mein großer Bruder hilft mir immer.
sentences.translation: My big brother always helps me.

sentences.text: Meine Brüder sind älter als ich.
sentences.translation: My brothers are older than me.

gloss: about it; on it (with verbs like denken an)
notes: Replaces an + it/that. Spoken short form: dran. Du bist dran = It's your turn.

sentences.text: Daran kann ich mich nicht erinnern.

sentences.translation: There's still something stuck to it.

notes: Vielen Dank = Thank you very much. Gott sei Dank = Thank God.

sentences.translation: Thanks a lot for the meal!

sentences.text: Gott sei Dank, du bist hier.

notes: Comparative of gern: Ich trinke lieber Tee = I prefer tea.

sentences.text: Das sage ich ihm lieber nicht.
sentences.translation: I'd rather not tell him that.

notes: auf jeden Fall = definitely; auf keinen Fall = no way.

sentences.text: Auf keinen Fall gehe ich da hin.
sentences.translation: There's no way I'm going there.

sentences.text: In diesem Fall bleiben wir zu Hause.
sentences.translation: In that case we'll stay at home.

sentences.text: Das ist nicht in allen Fällen so.
sentences.translation: That's not so in all cases.

gloss: all the same; (es ist mir egal) I don't care
notes: Never takes an ending. Egal! = Whatever!

gloss: to know (a person or place), be familiar with
notes: kennen = to know someone; wissen = to know a fact.

sentences.translation: How do you know each other?

notes: du vergisst, er vergisst; past vergaß, vergessen.
Echt? = Really?
Softens a question: Wer bist du eigentlich? = Who are you, anyway?

sentences.translation: What are you actually doing here?

sentences.text: Ich wollte eigentlich nach Hause gehen.
sentences.translation: I actually wanted to go home.

notes: Wie viel Uhr ist es? = What time is it? um acht Uhr = at eight o'clock.

sentences.text: Wir treffen uns um drei Uhr.

notes: Plural: Städte. in die Stadt gehen = to go into town.
Plural: Babys.

sentences.text: Babys weinen oft in der Nacht.

notes: du fährst, er fährt; past fuhr; perfect with sein: ich bin gefahren.

sentences.text: Wir sind mit dem Zug gefahren.

notes: Like Junge: der Name, den Namen. Mein Name ist … = My name is …
Not "become" (that is werden). Past bekam, perfect bekommen.

sentences.text: Ich bekomme jeden Tag viele Nachrichten.
sentences.translation: I get a lot of messages every day.

notes: Plural: Köpfe. Kopf hoch! = Chin up!

sentences.text: Das geht mir nicht aus dem Kopf.
sentences.translation: I can't get it out of my head.

notes: Comparative: kleiner.

sentences.text: Wir wohnen in einem kleinen Dorf.
sentences.translation: We live in a small village.

notes: Bis später! = See you later!

sentences.text: Zwei Tage später kam er zurück.
sentences.translation: Two days later he came back.

notes: Viel Glück! = Good luck! Glück haben = to be lucky.
letzte Woche = last week; zum letzten Mal = for the last time.

gloss: on it; for it (with verbs like warten auf)
notes: Replaces auf + it/that: Ich warte darauf = I'm waiting for it. Spoken: drauf.

sentences.translation: I'm not in the mood for that.

notes: am Ende = in the end; zu Ende = over.

sentences.translation: In the end everything was fine.

notes: Bis bald! = See you soon!

Plural: Dinge.

sentences.text: Was ist das für ein Ding?
sentences.translation: What kind of thing is that?

sentences.text: Es gibt Dinge, die ich nicht verstehe.
sentences.translation: There are things I don't understand.
We talk about lots of things.

gloss: to mean; to think (have an opinion)
notes: Was meinst du? = What do you mean? / What do you think? Not to be confused with mein (my).

sentences.translation: What do you mean by that?

sentences.text: So habe ich das nicht gemeint.
sentences.translation: I didn't mean it like that.

notes: Toll! = Great!
Counting: eins, zwei, drei. Before a noun: ein, eine.

sentences.translation: The score is one to nothing.

notes: Plural: Minuten.

sentences.text: Ich bin in fünf Minuten da.
sentences.translation: I'll be there in five minutes.

notes: Bist du bereit? = Are you ready? Usually after sein.

sentences.text: Er ist bereit, uns zu helfen.

notes: Wie weit ist es? = How far is it?

sentences.text: Wie weit ist es bis zum Bahnhof?
sentences.translation: How far is it to the station?

sentences.text: Das ist nicht weit von hier.

notes: Keine Ahnung! = No idea!

sentences.text: Hast du eine Ahnung, wo er ist?
sentences.translation: Do you have any idea where he is?
I don't know anything about it.

notes: Usually ein bisschen: ein bisschen Zeit = a little time.
Plural: Türen.
Plural: Autos.

sentences.translation: There are lots of cars here.

notes: The possessive of ihr (you all): euer Haus, eure Mutter.
Plural: Augen.

sentences.translation: I've got something in my eye.

notes: Singular in German: Die Polizei ist da = The police are here.
du stirbst, er stirbt; past starb; perfect with sein: ist gestorben.

sentences.text: Sein Großvater ist letztes Jahr gestorben.

notes: Location: Er ist draußen. Movement out: raus.
Not "fast" (quick); that is schnell.
Komm runter! = Come down!

sentences.text: Nimm die Füße vom Tisch runter!
sentences.translation: Take your feet off the table!

notes: Es ist vorbei = It's over. vorbeikommen = to drop by.
du triffst, er trifft; past traf, getroffen. sich treffen = to meet up.

sentences.translation: She met him in the park.

notes: Noun: die Arbeit.

sentences.text: Wir haben den ganzen Tag gearbeitet.

notes: Bist du verrückt? = Are you crazy?

sentences.translation: The children are driving me crazy.

notes: Was gibt's Neues? = What's new?

sentences.translation: Do you have a new job?

notes: With dative for place, accusative for movement.

sentences.text: Stell das Fahrrad hinter das Haus.
sentences.translation: Put the bike behind the house.

sentences.text: Mach die Tür hinter dir zu.

notes: Mach dir keine Sorgen = Don't worry.

sentences.text: Ich mache mir Sorgen um dich.
Meine einzige Sorge ist das Geld.

notes: der einzige Weg = the only way.

sentences.text: Du bist die einzige Person hier.

notes: Darum! = Because! (no explanation). es geht darum = it's about.

sentences.text: Es geht darum, wer recht hat.

notes: Plural: Töchter.

sentences.text: Ihre Tochter ist fünf Jahre alt.
sentences.translation: Her daughter is five years old.

notes: Plural: Ideen. Gute Idee! = Good idea!

sentences.translation: Do you have any other ideas?

notes: Plural: Schwestern.

sentences.text: Ich gehe mit meiner Schwester essen.
sentences.translation: I'm going out to eat with my sister.

notes: Was ist da drin? = What's in there?

sentences.translation: Is there any coffee left in it?

notes: Sei ruhig! = Be quiet! Bleib ruhig! = Stay calm!

sentences.text: Wir wohnen in einer ruhigen Straße.
sentences.translation: We live on a quiet street.

notes: Wie spät ist es? = What time is it? Comparative: später.

sentences.text: Tut mir leid, ich bin zu spät.

notes: ziemlich gut = pretty good.
Er hat sogar gelacht = He even laughed.
Warte kurz! = Wait a moment!

sentences.text: Ich habe nur eine kurze Frage.
sentences.translation: I just have a quick question.

notes: Informal. Plural: Kerle.

sentences.text: Die Kerle da drüben sind sehr laut.
sentences.translation: Those guys over there are very loud.

gloss: to lie (be lying); to be located
notes: Past lag, gelegen. Das liegt an dir = That's down to you.

sentences.text: Dein Handy liegt auf dem Tisch.
sentences.translation: Your phone is on the table.
The village is on the lake.

sentences.text: Wir lagen den ganzen Tag am Strand.
sentences.translation: We lay on the beach all day.

notes: Ich suche meinen Schlüssel = I'm looking for my key.

sentences.translation: What are you looking for here?
The police are looking for him.

notes: Hast du je …? = Have you ever …? je mehr, desto besser = the more, the better.

sentences.text: Hast du je so etwas gesehen?
sentences.translation: Have you ever seen anything like that?

sentences.text: Das kostet zwei Euro je Stück.

notes: Woher kommst du? = Where are you from? Woher weißt du das? = How do you know?

sentences.text: Ich weiß nicht, woher er kommt.
sentences.translation: I don't know where he's from.

notes: Adverb: lange (for a long time). Comparative: länger.
Informal; more formal: die Stelle or die Arbeit.
Also for instruments and roles: Gitarre spielen.

sentences.translation: The children are playing in the garden.

sentences.text: Wir haben die ganze Nacht gespielt.

notes: überhaupt nicht = not at all. Wer bist du überhaupt? = Who are you anyway?
Plural also Teufel. Was zum Teufel …? = What the hell …?

sentences.text: Was zum Teufel machst du da?
sentences.translation: What the hell are you doing there?

notes: Past verlor, verloren.

sentences.text: Sie verlor ihr Handy im Zug.
sentences.translation: She lost her phone on the train.

notes: Comparative größer, superlative am größten.

sentences.text: Mein Bruder ist größer als ich.
sentences.translation: My brother is taller than me.

notes: Plural: Hände.

sentences.text: Was hast du in der Hand?
sentences.translation: What have you got in your hand?

notes: Plural: Gründe. aus diesem Grund = for this reason.

sentences.text: Es gibt keinen Grund zur Sorge.

notes: Familiar; formal: Mutter.
Ruhe! = Quiet! Lass mich in Ruhe! = Leave me alone!

sentences.translation: I need a bit of peace and quiet.

notes: Adjective: tot (dead).

sentences.text: Nach seinem Tod war alles anders.
sentences.translation: After his death everything was different.

sentences.text: Sie hat Angst vor dem Tod.
Es geht um Leben und Tod.
sentences.translation: It's a matter of life and death.

notes: Plural: Stunden.

sentences.translation: I've been waiting for an hour.

sentences.text: In einer Stunde bin ich da.
sentences.translation: I'll be there in an hour.

notes: Ich hoffe es = I hope so.

sentences.text: Ich hoffe, es geht dir gut.

notes: nach oben = up(wards); da oben = up there.

sentences.text: Er ist oben in seinem Zimmer.

notes: gestern Abend = last night.
Ich versuche es = I'll try.
eine Art … = a kind of …; auf diese Art = this way.

sentences.text: Was für eine Art Musik magst du?
sentences.translation: What kind of music do you like?

sentences.text: Es gibt viele Arten von Brot.
sentences.translation: There are many kinds of bread.

notes: Schatz is a common way to say darling or honey.

sentences.translation: They're looking for an old treasure.

notes: Endlich! = Finally!

gloss: about, approximately; (in questions) by any chance
notes: In a question it shows surprise: Bist du etwa müde? = You're not tired, are you?

sentences.text: Er ist etwa so groß wie ich.
sentences.translation: He's about as tall as me.
